data.description:
## Observed — a near-miss, caught by luck

Two independent agent sessions on this host both redirected `make verify` output to the **same
hardcoded path**, `/tmp/verify2.log`:

- session in worktree `fix-pinned-view-packed` (analysing a contended verify run)
- session in worktree `fix-caused-by-lagging-checkout`

The second session's redirect **rewrote bytes inside the first session's log after that run had
already finished**. The mtime was five minutes later than the first session's own rc file — which is
the only reason it was noticed at all.

The first session's conclusion survived, but only by accident: it re-derived its failure census
scoped to the region after the last `short test summary info` marker, and the file happened to hold
exactly one summary block with exactly 14 entries matching its own reported total, so the collision
had struck only low offsets. Its own words: **"it stood by luck, not design."**

## Why this is worth a p2 rather than a shrug

The corrupted artifact was **evidence being used to decide whether `main` was broken**. A verify log
is not a scratch file; it is what an agent reads to decide "is this a real test failure or host
congestion", and that decision determines whether someone re-runs, files a bug, or blocks a change.
Silently interleaving two sessions' bytes into one such file can produce a census that is internally
consistent and wrong — the worst failure mode available, because nothing looks broken.

It is also **not rare by construction**. Six heavyweight consumers were observed on this host
simultaneously: three concurrent `make verify` runs (`fix-pinned-view-packed`,
`fix-alias-resolve-scan`, `fix-caused-by-lagging-checkout`) plus three `rebar review-plan` gates.
Any convention that names a fixed `/tmp` file collides the moment two of them overlap, and this
project routinely runs many sessions and worktrees at once.

## Related but distinct

`16e1` covered nested pytest destroying other sessions' **temp roots**. This is the sibling problem
one level up: explicit, hand-written redirect paths in agent commands and docs, not pytest's
tmp-root machinery. Fixing one does not fix the other.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 The guidance agents actually read (`AGENTS.md`, and any skill or runbook that shows a
      `> /tmp/<name>.log` redirect) prescribes a **per-session** scratch location rather than a fixed
      `/tmp` filename, with a concrete worked example an agent can copy verbatim. The failure being
      prevented — one session overwriting another's evidence — is stated, because a convention whose
      reason is unstated gets "simplified" back.
- [ ] AC2 A tree sweep enumerates every hardcoded `/tmp/<fixed-name>` redirect in committed docs,
      skills, scripts and runbooks, and each is either changed to a per-session path or explicitly
      justified as collision-safe. Record the sweep output so the residual set is auditable.
- [ ] AC3 Where the repo's own tooling writes such files, it derives the path from something unique
      per invocation (pid, session id, or mktemp) rather than a literal. Prove it with a test that
      runs the writer twice concurrently and asserts the two outputs are distinct files.
- [ ] AC4 `[non-codebase]` Confirm on a real host that two overlapping `make verify` runs from
      different worktrees no longer write to a shared path, by listing the actual files each
      produced.
      provenance: environment=<v>; principal=<v>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <justification>

## Explicitly out of scope

The 4-slot gate semaphore contention itself. That is a separate, already-known problem — this ticket
is only about two writers naming the same file. Fixing the semaphore would reduce how often the
collision window opens but would not close it.

## Constraints

Never use `--force` or any gate bypass. `timeout` does not exist on this macOS host (it exits 127, a
silent no-op) — bound with `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'`. Do not touch the shared main checkout;
do not `git stash` anywhere.
data.title: Concurrent sessions collide on hardcoded /tmp log paths, silently corrupting each other's evidence
